records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗ית בַּֽחֲמִשִׁי֙ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ בָּ֧אוּ אֲנָשִׁ֛ים מִזִּקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לִדְרֹ֣שׁ אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ לְפָנָֽי׃ס
records.gloss: And it was in the year the seventh, in the fifth, on the tenth of the month, came men from [the] elders of Israel to inquire of Yahweh, and they sat before me.
pieces: In the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, a group of Israel's elders came to consult {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they sat down in front of me.

L.1: And it came about in the seventh year, in the fifth [month], on the tenth of the month, [that] men from the elders of Israel came in to inquire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they sat before me.

R.1: On the tenth day of the fifth month, in the seventh year of our exile, some of the elders of Israel came to ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for a message. They sat down in front of me.

decisions.choice: the seventh year, the fifth month, the tenth day: counted from King Jehoiachin's exile, about August 591 BC
decisions.reason: Ezekiel dates his visions by the years since King Jehoiachin was taken to Babylon in 597 BC (1:2; 8:1). The seventh year of that exile, in the fifth month, falls in the summer of 591 BC, eleven months after the vision of 8:1 and about five years before Jerusalem fell (33:21).

decisions.choice: to inquire of the LORD: to ask for a word from the LORD through his prophet
decisions.reason: To "inquire of the LORD" was to come to a prophet for God's answer to a question or a need (1 Kings 22:7-8; 2 Kings 22:13-18). Elders of the exiles had come to Ezekiel in the same way in 8:1 and 14:1. The chapter does not say what they asked; the LORD's answer is that he will not be consulted by them (verses 3 and 31).

decisions.choice: in the seventh year of our exile
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives only the number of the year. Readable says what the years are counted from (m1), and puts the day and month first, as people say a date.

records.heading: Elders come to consult {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And was [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.2: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: the formula as in Jeremiah; the LORD's words that follow take no quotation marks
alternatives: quotation marks around the whole of the LORD's speech
decisions.reason: "The word of the LORD came to me, saying" keeps the wording set for Jeremiah at each level. Everything from verse 3 to the end of the chapter is the LORD's own speech. As in Isaiah and the other prophets, God's first-person speech takes no quotation marks; words quoted inside it, such as what God once said to Israel or what the people say, take double quotes.

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶת־זִקְנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הֲלִדְרֹ֥שׁ אֹתִ֖י אַתֶּ֣ם בָּאִ֑ים חַי־אָ֨נִי֙ אִם־אִדָּרֵ֣שׁ לָכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: Son of man, speak to [the] elders of Israel and say to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Is [it] to inquire of me [that] you [are] coming? [As] I live, I will not be inquired of by you, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel. Say to them, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Have you come to consult {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? As surely as I live, I will not let you consult {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.3: Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel and say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Is it to inquire of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [that] you are coming? As I live, I will not be inquired of by you, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.3: Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel. Tell them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Have you come to ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for a message? As surely as I live, I will not answer you, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: son of man: a human being, a mortal addressed by God
decisions.reason: This is how God addresses Ezekiel throughout the book. It means "human being" and stresses that the prophet is a mortal before God; see the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: As I live: an oath by God's own life
decisions.reason: God swears by his own life, the surest oath there is (Numbers 14:21, 28; Deuteronomy 32:40). The same oath closes the answer in verse 31 and opens the threat of verse 33.

decisions.choice: I will not be inquired of by you: God refuses to give these elders an answer
decisions.reason: The verb form means "let myself be sought" or "answer when sought". God refused in the same way in 14:3, because the elders had set up idols in their hearts. Here the reason is the history of rebellion that the chapter sets out, which, God says, they are still repeating (verses 30-31).

decisions.choice: consult (B); ask for a message (R)
decisions.reason: "Inquire of" is kept at Literal. Balanced and Readable use everyday words for coming to a prophet for God's answer (verse 1, m2). Readable says "I will not answer you", which is what the refusal means. The oath "As I live" is "As surely as I live" at Balanced and Readable, as in Jeremiah 22:24.

records.source: הֲתִשְׁפֹּ֣ט אֹתָ֔ם הֲתִשְׁפּ֖וֹט בֶּן־אָדָ֑ם אֶת־תּוֹעֲבֹ֥ת אֲבוֹתָ֖ם הוֹדִיעֵֽם׃
records.gloss: Will you judge them, will you judge, son of man? [The] abominations of their fathers make known to them.
pieces: Will you judge them? Will you judge them, son of man? Then make them see the detestable practices of their {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}.

L.4: Will you judge them? Will you judge, son of man? Make known to them the abominations of their fathers.

R.4: Son of man, are you ready to judge them? Then make them face the disgusting things their {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} did.

decisions.choice: Will you judge them?: a call to bring the charge against them, in effect a command
alternatives: a question asking whether Ezekiel is willing to plead for them
decisions.reason: The repeated question invites the prophet to act as the one who states the case against the people, and the command that follows says how: by telling them what their ancestors did. Ezekiel is asked the same thing about Jerusalem in 22:2 and about Oholah and Oholibah in 23:36.

decisions.choice: abominations: practices the LORD finds detestable, above all idol worship
decisions.reason: The word is used throughout Ezekiel for idolatry and the acts that go with it (5:9, 11; 8:6). Verses 5-31 now list them, from Egypt to Ezekiel's own day.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the earlier generations of the people, women as well as men, so Balanced and Readable say "ancestors", with "fathers" as the reader's alternative. Literal keeps "fathers".

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ בְּיוֹם֙ בָּחֳרִ֣י בְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וָאֶשָּׂ֣א יָדִ֗י לְזֶ֨רַע֙ בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וָאִוָּדַ֥ע לָהֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וָאֶשָּׂ֨א יָדִ֤י לָהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And say to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: On [the] day of my choosing Israel, and I lifted my hand to [the] seed of [the] house of Jacob, and I made myself known to them in [the] land of Egypt, and I lifted my hand to them, saying, I [am] Yahweh your God.
pieces: Say to them, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: On the day I chose Israel, I raised {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand in an oath to the offspring of Jacob's house and made {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} known to them in the land of Egypt. I raised {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand in an oath to them and said, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God."

L.5: And say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: On the day when I chose Israel, I lifted {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to the seed of the house of Jacob, and I made {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} known to them in the land of Egypt; I lifted {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to them, saying, "I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God."

R.5: Tell them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: When I chose Israel, I made a solemn promise to the people of Jacob's family. I showed them who I am while they were in Egypt. I promised them with an oath, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God."

decisions.choice: I lifted my hand: I swore an oath
decisions.reason: Raising the hand was the gesture of swearing (Genesis 14:22; Deuteronomy 32:40). Exodus 6:8 uses the same words for God's oath to give the land to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. The phrase runs through the chapter: God swears to bring Israel out (verse 6), later swears that the rebels will not enter the land (verse 15) and that he will scatter them (verse 23), and keeps his oath to the ancestors (verses 28 and 42).

decisions.choice: "I am the LORD your God": the words of God's self-revelation in Egypt
decisions.reason: In Egypt God told Moses to say to Israel, "I am the LORD", and promised, "I will be your God" (Exodus 6:2-8); the Ten Commandments open with "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt" (Exodus 20:2). Ezekiel retells that moment as the start of Israel's story with God.

decisions.choice: chose: God's choice of Israel as his people
decisions.reason: This is the only place where Ezekiel says that God "chose" Israel. The word recalls Deuteronomy, where God chose Israel out of all peoples because he loved them (Deuteronomy 7:6-8).

decisions.choice: raised my hand in an oath (B); made a solemn promise, promised with an oath (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the gesture. Balanced names it as an oath the first time and says "swore" after that; Readable says "promised with an oath", the wording of Exodus 6:8 at Readable.

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא נָשָׂ֤אתִי יָדִי֙ לָהֶ֔ם לְהֽוֹצִיאָ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֶל־אֶ֜רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־תַּ֣רְתִּי לָהֶ֗ם זָבַ֤ת חָלָב֙ וּדְבַ֔שׁ צְבִ֥י הִ֖יא לְכָל־הָאֲרָצֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: On the day the that I lifted my hand to them to bring them out from [the] land of Egypt to a land that I had searched out for them, flowing [with] milk and honey; beauty it [is] to all the lands.
pieces: On that day I swore to them that I would bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land I had scouted out for them, flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands.

L.6: On that day I lifted {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to them, to bring them out from the land of Egypt to a land that I had scouted out for them, flowing [with] milk and honey; it [is the] beauty of all the lands.

R.6: That day I promised them with an oath that I would bring them out of Egypt. I would take them to a land I had chosen for them. It was a rich and fertile land, full of milk and honey, the most beautiful land of all.

decisions.choice: scouted out: explored, as a scout explores a land
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the spies Moses sent to explore Canaan (Numbers 13:2, 16-17). Here God himself has explored the land in advance and picked it for Israel, as he went ahead of them "to scout out a place" for their camps (Deuteronomy 1:33).

decisions.choice: flowing with milk and honey: the promise of Exodus 3:8
decisions.reason: The phrase is the standard description of the promised land from God's first words to Moses (Exodus 3:8, 17). Milk points to good pasture for flocks, and honey to wild bees' honey or a syrup from fruit; together they picture a rich and fertile country.

decisions.choice: the beauty of all the lands: the finest land of all
decisions.reason: The word means beauty or splendor. Jeremiah 3:19 calls Israel's land "the most beautiful inheritance of the nations", and Daniel 8:9 and 11:16 call it "the beautiful land".

decisions.choice: a land I had chosen for them; a rich and fertile land, full of milk and honey
alternatives: a land I had scouted out for them, flowing with milk and honey
decisions.reason: Readable says what God's searching out meant for Israel, and uses the Readable wording of Exodus 3:8 for the milk and honey.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם אִ֣ישׁ שִׁקּוּצֵ֤י עֵינָיו֙ הַשְׁלִ֔יכוּ וּבְגִלּוּלֵ֥י מִצְרַ֖יִם אַל־תִּטַּמָּ֑אוּ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I said to them, Each [man] the detestable things of his eyes throw away, and with [the] idols of Egypt do not defile yourselves; I [am] Yahweh your God.
pieces: I said to them, "Every one of you must throw away the vile idols you look to, and do not make yourselves unclean with the idols of Egypt. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God."

L.7: And I said to them, "Each [of you], throw away the detestable things of his eyes, and do not defile yourselves with the filthy idols of Egypt; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God."

R.7: I told them, "Each of you must throw away the disgusting idols you love to look at. Do not make yourselves unclean by worshiping the idols of Egypt. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God."

decisions.choice: the idols of Egypt: Israel worshiped Egypt's gods while still in Egypt
decisions.reason: The book of Exodus does not tell of Israel worshiping idols in Egypt, but Joshua 24:14 tells the people to put away "the gods your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt", and the golden calf (Exodus 32) shows how ready they were to make one. Ezekiel returns to Israel's idolatry in Egypt in 23:3, 8, 19 and 27.

decisions.choice: the detestable things of his eyes: the idols each person looked to with desire and devotion
decisions.reason: To lift one's eyes to an idol is to look to it for help and to worship it (18:6, 12, 15). The "detestable things" are the idols themselves, a word Ezekiel uses with contempt (5:11; 7:20).

decisions.choice: idols: Ezekiel's scornful word for idols
decisions.reason: The word for idols here is the one Ezekiel uses most often, a word of contempt; see the note at 6:4.

decisions.choice: the vile idols you look to (B); the disgusting idols you love to look at (R)
alternatives: the detestable things of his eyes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the detestable things are idols, as the book's word list sets out, and turn "of his eyes" into the looking it means (m2). Readable adds "by worshiping" to say how the idols make them unclean.

records.source: וַיַּמְרוּ־בִ֗י וְלֹ֤א אָבוּ֙ לִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ אֵלַ֔י אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־שִׁקּוּצֵ֤י עֵֽינֵיהֶם֙ לֹ֣א הִשְׁלִ֔יכוּ וְאֶת־גִּלּוּלֵ֥י מִצְרַ֖יִם לֹ֣א עָזָ֑בוּ וָאֹמַ֞ר לִשְׁפֹּ֧ךְ חֲמָתִ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם לְכַלּ֤וֹת אַפִּי֙ בָּהֶ֔ם בְּת֖וֹךְ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: But they rebelled against me and were not willing to listen to me; each [man] the detestable things of their eyes they did not throw away, and the idols of Egypt they did not forsake. And I said to pour out my wrath on them, to spend my anger on them in [the] midst of [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: But they rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and refused to listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. None of them threw away the vile idols they looked to, and they did not abandon the idols of Egypt. So I said that I would pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on them and use up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger against them there in the land of Egypt.

L.8: But they rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and were not willing to listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; they did not, each one, throw away the detestable things of their eyes, and they did not forsake the filthy idols of Egypt. Then I said [that I would] pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on them, to spend {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on them there in the midst of the land of Egypt.

R.8: But they rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and would not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Not one of them threw away the disgusting idols they loved to look at. They kept on worshiping the idols of Egypt. So I said I would pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on them and punish them fully while they were still in Egypt.

decisions.choice: pour out my wrath, spend my anger: let anger run its full course
decisions.reason: To "spend" anger is to use it up, to punish until nothing of it is left. Ezekiel uses the same pair of phrases in 5:13, 7:8 and 20:21.

decisions.choice: I said: God's intention, which he did not carry out
decisions.reason: "I said" here means "I thought" or "I resolved". The next verse tells why God held back. The same pattern of rebellion, resolve and restraint returns in verses 13-14 and 21-22.

decisions.choice: punish them fully
decisions.reason: Readable says what spending anger means (m1).

records.source: וָאַ֨עַשׂ֙ לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמִ֔י לְבִלְתִּ֥י הֵחֵ֛ל לְעֵינֵ֥י הַגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֣מָּה בְתוֹכָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר נוֹדַ֤עְתִּי אֲלֵיהֶם֙ לְעֵ֣ינֵיהֶ֔ם לְהוֹצִיאָ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: But I acted for the sake of my name, so as not to be profaned in [the] eyes of the nations among whom they [were], in whose eyes I made myself known to them, by bringing them out from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: But I acted for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, to keep it from being dishonored in the eyes of the nations they lived among, the nations in whose sight I had made {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} known to Israel by bringing them out of the land of Egypt.

L.9: But I acted for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, that it might not be profaned in the eyes of the nations in whose midst they [were], before whose eyes I made {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} known to them by bringing them out of the land of Egypt.

R.9: But I acted to protect the honor of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. I did not want the nations around them to treat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name with scorn. Those nations had seen {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} show Israel who I am when I brought them out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: for the sake of my name: to guard God's reputation among the nations
decisions.reason: God's "name" is his known character and honor. If he had destroyed Israel after rescuing it so publicly, the nations would have concluded that he could not or would not keep his word. Moses pleads in just these terms in Exodus 32:12 and Numbers 14:13-16. The refrain returns in verses 14, 22 and 44.

decisions.choice: profaned: treated as common, dishonored
decisions.reason: To profane is to treat what is holy as ordinary. The same verb is used of the Sabbaths in verses 13, 16, 21 and 24, and in 36:20-23 God's name is profaned among the nations by Israel's exile.

decisions.choice: dishonored (B); treat ... with scorn (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "profaned", the word of holy and common. Balanced and Readable say what profaning a name means for those who hear it.

records.source: וָאֽוֹצִיאֵ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וָאֲבִאֵ֖ם אֶל־הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃
records.gloss: And I brought them out from [the] land of Egypt and brought them into the wilderness.
pieces: So I led them out of the land of Egypt and took them into the wilderness.

L.10: So I brought them out from the land of Egypt and led them into the wilderness.

R.10: So I led them out of Egypt and into the desert.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: the journey from Egypt to Sinai and beyond
decisions.reason: The wilderness is where God gave the law at Sinai (verse 11; Exodus 19-20). It is also where Israel rebelled (verses 13-26), and in verses 35-36 God will lead the exiles into a new "wilderness" for judgment.

records.source: וָאֶתֵּ֤ן לָהֶם֙ אֶת־חֻקּוֹתַ֔י וְאֶת־מִשְׁפָּטַ֖י הוֹדַ֣עְתִּי אוֹתָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אוֹתָ֛ם הָאָדָ֖ם וָחַ֥י בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I gave to them my statutes, and my ordinances I made known to them, which does them the person and lives by them.
pieces: I gave them {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and taught them {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings. The one who does them will live by them.

L.11: And I gave them {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments I made known to them, which a person shall do and he shall live by them.

R.11: I gave them {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and taught them {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules. Anyone who obeys them will have life because of them.

decisions.choice: which a person shall do and live by them: the words of Leviticus 18:5
decisions.reason: Leviticus 18:5 says that God's statutes and judgments are those "which a person shall do and he shall live by them". Ezekiel repeats the phrase in verses 13 and 21, and in 18:9 and 33:19 he uses the same promise of life for the person who does what is right. Nehemiah 9:29 quotes it, and Paul cites it in Romans 10:5 and Galatians 3:12.

decisions.choice: live: enjoy life under God's blessing in the land
decisions.reason: In the law, life is the gift that comes with obeying God and death the result of turning from him (Deuteronomy 30:15-20). The rest of the chapter sets the life these laws offer against the "statutes that were not good", by which the people could not live (verse 25).

decisions.choice: statutes and judgments (L); statutes and rulings (B); laws and rules (R); the wording of Leviticus 18:5
decisions.reason: The two words for God's commands, and the promise attached to them, keep the wording of Leviticus 18:5 at each level, because Ezekiel quotes it. The same wording is used throughout the chapter.

records.source: וְגַ֤ם אֶת־שַׁבְּתוֹתַי֙ נָתַ֣תִּי לָהֶ֔ם לִהְי֣וֹת לְא֔וֹת בֵּינִ֖י וּבֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם לָדַ֕עַת כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מְקַדְּשָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And also my sabbaths I gave to them, to be for a sign between me and between them, to know that I [am] Yahweh who sanctifies them.
pieces: I also gave them {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths as a sign between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and them, so that they would know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the one who sets them apart as holy.

L.12: And also {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths I gave to them, to be for a sign between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and them, in order that [they might] know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who sanctifies them.

R.12: I also gave them {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbath days. They were a sign between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and them. They showed that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who has made them {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own holy people.

decisions.choice: the Sabbaths as a sign: the words of Exodus 31:13
decisions.reason: Exodus 31:13 says that God's Sabbaths are "a sign between me and you ... that you may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you". Ezekiel repeats it almost word for word. Because the Sabbath marked Israel as God's people, profaning it is named again and again in this chapter (verses 13, 16, 21, 24).

decisions.choice: sanctifies: sets apart as holy, as God's own
decisions.reason: To sanctify is to make holy, set apart for God. God, not the people, is the one who makes Israel holy; the Sabbath is the sign of it.

decisions.choice: the wording of Exodus 31:13 at each level; "Sabbaths" capitalized
decisions.reason: Because Ezekiel quotes Exodus 31:13, each level uses that verse's wording, with the person changed to "them".

records.source: וַיַּמְרוּ־בִ֨י בֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר בְּחֻקּוֹתַ֨י לֹא־הָלָ֜כוּ וְאֶת־מִשְׁפָּטַ֣י מָאָ֗סוּ אֲשֶׁר֩ יַעֲשֶׂ֨ה אֹתָ֤ם הָֽאָדָם֙ וָחַ֣י בָּהֶ֔ם וְאֶת־שַׁבְּתֹתַ֖י חִלְּל֣וּ מְאֹ֑ד וָאֹמַ֞ר לִשְׁפֹּ֨ךְ חֲמָתִ֧י עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר לְכַלּוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And rebelled against me [the] house of Israel in the wilderness; in my statutes they did not walk, and my ordinances they rejected, which does them the person and lives by them; and my sabbaths they profaned greatly. And I said to pour out my wrath on them in the wilderness to finish them off.
pieces: But in the wilderness the house of Israel rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They did not follow {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes; they rejected {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings, though the one who does them will live by them, and they utterly dishonored {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths. So I said that I would pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on them in the wilderness and destroy them completely.

L.13: But the house of Israel rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the wilderness: in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes they did not walk, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments they rejected, which a person shall do and he shall live by them, and they profaned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths greatly. Then I said [that I would] pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath upon them in the wilderness, so as to finish them.

R.13: But the people of Israel rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the desert. They did not live by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws. They rejected {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules, even though anyone who obeys them will have life because of them. They treated {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbath days with no respect at all. So I said I would pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on them there in the desert and destroy them.

decisions.choice: rebellion in the wilderness: the golden calf, the refusal to enter the land, the broken Sabbath
decisions.reason: After the golden calf God said he would destroy the people (Exodus 32:10), and again after they refused to enter the land (Numbers 14:11-12). Some gathered manna on the Sabbath (Exodus 16:27-28), and a man was found gathering wood on it (Numbers 15:32-36).

decisions.choice: profaned greatly: treated the holy day as an ordinary one, over and over
decisions.reason: See verse 9. To profane the Sabbath was to work on it and treat it as any other day (Exodus 31:14; Jeremiah 17:21-27).

decisions.choice: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: "House of Israel" means the people of Israel as one family. Readable says "the people of Israel" throughout the chapter.

records.source: וָאֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמִ֑י לְבִלְתִּ֤י הֵחֵל֙ לְעֵינֵ֣י הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹצֵאתִ֖ים לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃

L.14: But I acted for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, that it might not be profaned in the eyes of the nations before whose eyes I had brought them out.

R.14: But I acted to protect the honor of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. I did not want it treated with scorn by the nations who had seen {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} bring Israel out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: the refrain of verse 9: Moses' plea for the people
decisions.reason: When God said he would destroy the people at Kadesh, Moses answered that the Egyptians and the nations would hear of it and say that the LORD could not bring his people into the land (Numbers 14:13-16). The refrain of verse 9 returns here and in verse 22.

decisions.choice: bring Israel out of Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable names the people and the place, which the Hebrew leaves to the context.

pieces: Also, in the wilderness, I swore an oath to them that I would not lead them into the land I had given them, flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands,

L.15: And also I lifted {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to them in the wilderness not to bring them into the land that I had given [them], flowing [with] milk and honey; it [is the] beauty of all the lands,

R.15: In the desert I also made a solemn promise to them. I promised that I would not bring them into the land I had given them. It was a rich and fertile land, full of milk and honey, the most beautiful land of all.

decisions.choice: the oath that the wilderness generation would not enter the land
decisions.reason: At Kadesh God swore that none of the adults who had rebelled would enter the land, except Caleb and Joshua (Numbers 14:28-30; Psalm 95:11; 106:26). The oath that once promised the land (verse 6) now shuts them out of it.

decisions.choice: the land that I had given: the land already given by promise
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say to whom the land was given. It is the land God had promised to Israel, as the wording of verse 6 shows.

decisions.choice: given them
decisions.reason: The comma at Literal and Balanced shows that the sentence runs on into verse 16, which gives the reason for the oath. Readable makes two sentences and begins verse 16 with "I did this because".

records.source: יַ֜עַן בְּמִשְׁפָּטַ֣י מָאָ֗סוּ וְאֶת־חֻקּוֹתַי֙ לֹא־הָלְכ֣וּ בָהֶ֔ם וְאֶת־שַׁבְּתוֹתַ֖י חִלֵּ֑לוּ כִּ֛י אַחֲרֵ֥י גִלּוּלֵיהֶ֖ם לִבָּ֥ם הֹלֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: because my ordinances they rejected, and in my statutes they did not walk in them, and my sabbaths they profaned; for after their idols their heart [was] going.
pieces: because they rejected {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings, did not follow {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and dishonored {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths. Their hearts were set on their idols.

L.16: because they rejected {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments, and as for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes, they did not walk in them, and they profaned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths; for their heart went after their filthy idols.

R.16: I did this because they rejected {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules, did not live by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and treated {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbath days with no respect. They loved their idols with all their hearts.

decisions.choice: their heart went after their idols: their devotion belonged to their idols
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of will and desire. A heart that "goes after" idols has given them its loyalty (11:21; 33:31).

decisions.choice: I did this because
decisions.reason: Readable ends the long sentence of verse 15 and starts a new one here, so it names what the reason belongs to.

records.source: וַתָּ֧חָס עֵינִ֛י עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מִֽשַּׁחֲתָ֑ם וְלֹֽא־עָשִׂ֧יתִי אוֹתָ֛ם כָּלָ֖ה בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
records.gloss: But spared my eye on them from destroying them, and I did not make of them an end in the wilderness.
pieces: Yet I had pity on them and did not destroy them; I did not wipe them out in the wilderness.

L.17: Yet {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eye spared them from destroying them, and I did not make an end of them in the wilderness.

R.17: But I felt sorry for them and did not destroy them. I did not kill them all in the desert.

decisions.choice: my eye spared them: I had pity on them
decisions.reason: The eye shows what a person feels. Elsewhere Ezekiel has God say, "My eye will not spare, and I will have no pity" (5:11; 7:4, 9; 8:18; 9:10). Here, in Israel's early history, God's eye did spare.

decisions.choice: had pity on them (B); felt sorry for them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m1).

records.source: וָאֹמַ֤ר אֶל־בְּנֵיהֶם֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר בְּחוּקֵּ֤י אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ אַל־תֵּלֵ֔כוּ וְאֶת־מִשְׁפְּטֵיהֶ֖ם אַל־תִּשְׁמֹ֑רוּ וּבְגִלּוּלֵיהֶ֖ם אַל־תִּטַּמָּֽאוּ׃
records.gloss: And I said to their sons in the wilderness, In [the] statutes of your fathers do not walk, and their ordinances do not keep, and with their idols do not defile yourselves.
pieces: In the wilderness I said to their {{gender:children|sons}}, "Do not follow the statutes of your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} or keep their rulings, and do not make yourselves unclean with their idols.

L.18: And I said to their {{gender:children|sons}} in the wilderness, "Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers, and do not keep their judgments, and do not defile yourselves with their filthy idols.

R.18: In the desert I told their {{gender:children|sons}}, "Do not follow the ways of your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} or live by their rules. Do not make yourselves unclean by worshiping their idols.

decisions.choice: their children: the generation that grew up in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The children of those who left Egypt were the ones who would enter the land (Numbers 14:31; Deuteronomy 1:39). Deuteronomy is Moses' teaching to this second generation on the edge of the land.

decisions.choice: the statutes of your fathers: the customs the older generation lived by, set against God's statutes
decisions.reason: The same word that is used for God's statutes is used here for the ways of the parents. Verse 19 sets the two side by side: not their statutes, but mine.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means children of both sexes here, the whole next generation, so every level uses the inclusive word with "sons" as the alternative, as Exodus does for "the children of Israel". The quotation runs on to the end of verse 20.

records.gloss: I [am] Yahweh your God; in my statutes walk, and my ordinances keep and do them,

L.19: I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God; in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes walk, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments keep and do them,

R.19: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Live by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws. Be careful to obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules.

decisions.reason: Leviticus 18:4 and 19:37 join the same words: "keep my statutes and my judgments ... I am the LORD your God". God's statutes replace the statutes of the parents (verse 18).

L.20: and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths holy, and they will be for a sign between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you, so that [you will] know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God."

R.20: Treat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbath days as holy. They will be a sign between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you. They will show that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God."

decisions.choice: keep my Sabbaths holy; a sign between me and you: Exodus 20:8 and 31:13
decisions.reason: The command to keep the Sabbath holy is the fourth commandment (Exodus 20:8), and the sign is that of verse 12 (Exodus 31:13). Jeremiah 17:22 uses the same command.

decisions.choice: that you may know that I am the LORD your God: the book's refrain, here as the purpose of the Sabbath
decisions.reason: This is not the usual form of the refrain "you will know that I am the LORD", but a purpose clause, as in Exodus 31:13. Each level keeps the words of the refrain and the purpose: "that you may know" (L), "so that you will know" (B), "They will show that" (R).

They did not follow {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and were not careful to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings, though the one who does them will live by them. They dishonored {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths. So I said that I would pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on them and use up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger against them in the wilderness.

L.21: But the {{gender:children|sons}} rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes they did not walk, and they were not careful to do {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments, which a person shall do and he shall live by them; they profaned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths. Then I said [that I would] pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on them, to spend {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger against them in the wilderness.

They were not careful to obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules, even though anyone who obeys them will have life because of them. They treated {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbath days with no respect. So I said I would pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on them and punish them fully in the desert.

decisions.choice: the second generation's rebellion: Baal of Peor and the complaints on the way
decisions.reason: The children who were to enter the land also rebelled: they grumbled against God and Moses (Numbers 20:2-13; 21:4-9) and joined in the worship of the Baal of Peor (Numbers 25:1-9).

decisions.choice: too (B); also (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain that the children repeated their parents' rebellion, which the repeated wording of verses 13 and 21 shows in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: I held back my hand: I stopped myself from striking
decisions.reason: The hand is the power that strikes. To turn it back is to refrain from punishing (Lamentations 2:8 uses the opposite). The rest of the verse repeats verse 14 word for word.

records.source: גַּם־אֲנִ֗י נָשָׂ֧אתִי אֶת־יָדִ֛י לָהֶ֖ם בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר לְהָפִ֤יץ אֹתָם֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם וּלְזָר֥וֹת אוֹתָ֖ם בָּאֲרָצֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Also I lifted my hand to them in the wilderness, to scatter them among the nations and to disperse them in the lands,
pieces: In the wilderness I also swore to them that I would scatter them among the nations and spread them through the countries,

L.23: Also I lifted {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to them in the wilderness, to scatter them among the nations and to disperse them in the lands,

R.23: In the desert I also made a solemn promise to them. I promised that I would scatter them among the nations and spread them out through other countries.

decisions.choice: scattering among the nations: the threat of exile, already made in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The law warns, from the time of the wilderness, that a disobedient Israel would be scattered among the nations (Leviticus 26:33; Deuteronomy 28:64). Psalm 106:26-27 also speaks of God swearing in the wilderness to scatter them. For Ezekiel's hearers, already in exile, the oath has come true.

decisions.choice: the oath was sworn long before it was carried out
alternatives: an oath carried out at once
decisions.reason: The scattering did not happen in the wilderness; it came in Ezekiel's own time. Ezekiel's point is that the exile was not a sudden accident but the outcome of a long history that God had warned about from the start.

L.24: because they did not do {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments, and they rejected {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes, and they profaned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths, and their eyes were after the filthy idols of their fathers.

R.24: I did this because they did not obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules. They rejected {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and treated {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbath days with no respect. They longed for the idols their {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} had worshiped.

decisions.choice: their eyes were after the idols: they longed for them
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, the eyes stand for desire and devotion. The idols are those their parents had served, so each generation took up the sins of the one before (verse 30).

decisions.choice: I did this because
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, Readable starts a new sentence and names what the reason belongs to.

records.source: וְגַם־אֲנִי֙ נָתַ֣תִּי לָהֶ֔ם חֻקִּ֖ים לֹ֣א טוֹבִ֑ים וּמִ֨שְׁפָּטִ֔ים לֹ֥א יִֽחְי֖וּ בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And also I gave them statutes not good and ordinances [by which] they could not live by them,
pieces: I also gave them statutes that were not good and rulings by which they could not live.

L.25: And also I gave them statutes [that were] not good and judgments by which they could not live,

R.25: I also gave them laws that were not good, rules that could not give them life.

decisions.choice: statutes that were not good: given as a judgment on a people who had rejected the good statutes; the text does not say which statutes these are
alternatives: God handed them over to the customs and laws of the nations they chose to follow, as he "gave them over to the stubbornness of their heart" (Psalm 81:13)
a law God did give, that every firstborn belongs to him (Exodus 13:2, 12; 22:28), which in their idolatry they took as a demand for child sacrifice (verse 26)
bitter irony: the people treated the laws they made up as though God had given them
decisions.reason: Verse 25 answers verse 11: there God gave statutes by which a person lives, and here, after generations of rebellion, statutes by which they cannot live. Verse 26 ties these statutes to the offering of every firstborn, which verse 31 shows to be child sacrifice. Elsewhere the law forbids child sacrifice outright (Leviticus 18:21; Deuteronomy 12:31; 18:10), and in Jeremiah the LORD says that he never commanded it and it never came into his mind (Jeremiah 7:31; 19:5). So these are not God's good law; but the text does not explain how God "gave" them. Most readings take it as a judgment in which God gave the people up to what they had chosen, as he hardened Pharaoh's heart or as Romans 1:24-28 says that God "gave them up". The verse is one of the hardest in Ezekiel.

decisions.choice: not good ... could not live by them: the opposite of verse 11
decisions.reason: The words "live by them" repeat verses 11, 13 and 21 with a "not": these statutes bring death instead of life.

decisions.choice: gave, at every level
decisions.reason: Softer wording would decide the question that m1 leaves open, so every level says "gave", as the Hebrew does. The comma at Literal shows that the sentence runs on into verse 26.

records.source: וָאֲטַמֵּ֤א אוֹתָם֙ בְּמַתְּנוֹתָ֔ם בְּהַעֲבִ֖יר כָּל־פֶּ֣טֶר רָ֑חַם לְמַ֣עַן אֲשִׁמֵּ֔ם לְמַ֨עַן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵֽדְע֔וּ אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And I defiled them by their gifts, in making pass every opener of womb, in order that I might devastate them, in order that they would know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: I made them unclean through their own gifts, when they gave up every firstborn child as an offering, so that I might bring them to ruin, so that they would know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.26: and I defiled them through their gifts, when [they] handed over every first opener of the womb, so that I might devastate them, so that they would know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.26: I let their own gifts make them unclean when they sacrificed every firstborn child. I did this to ruin them, so that they would know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: every first opener of the womb: the firstborn, whom the law gave to God, here sacrificed
decisions.reason: Exodus 13:12 uses the same words: Israel was to "hand over" to the LORD every firstborn, and firstborn sons were to be redeemed with an offering in their place (Exodus 13:13-15; 34:19-20). The people turned this into giving their children to idols in the fire, as verse 31, 16:20-21 and 23:37 say.

decisions.choice: I defiled them: God let the people's own acts make them unclean, as a judgment
decisions.reason: Like verse 25, this speaks of God's judgment working through what the people chose. The gifts were "their" gifts, and in offering them they made themselves unclean.

decisions.choice: devastate them: ruin them, leaving them appalled
decisions.reason: The verb means to make desolate and also to stun with horror. Both senses fit: the sacrifices brought ruin on the people, and should have shocked them into seeing what they had become.

decisions.choice: handed over every first opener of the womb
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the wording of Exodus 13:12, which uses the same verb, so that the reader can see the law the people twisted. Balanced and Readable say what was done (m1).

decisions.choice: I let their own gifts make them unclean; so that they would know that I am the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the uncleanness came through the people's own offerings (m2). The book's refrain is kept in the purpose form the Hebrew has here, as in verse 20.

records.source: לָכֵ֞ן דַּבֵּ֨ר אֶל־בֵּ֤ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בֶּן־אָדָ֔ם וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה ע֗וֹד זֹ֚את גִּדְּפ֤וּ אוֹתִי֙ אֲב֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם בְּמַעֲלָ֥ם בִּ֖י מָֽעַל׃
records.gloss: Therefore speak to [the] house of Israel, son of man, and say to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Yet in this blasphemed me your fathers, in their acting treacherously against me [with] treachery.
pieces: Therefore, son of man, speak to the house of Israel and say to them, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: In this way too your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} insulted {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, by breaking faith with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.27: Therefore speak to the house of Israel, son of man, and say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: In this also your fathers blasphemed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, by acting faithlessly against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with faithlessness.

R.27: So, son of man, speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} also insulted {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} by being unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: blasphemed: insulted, reviled
decisions.reason: The verb means to speak or act against someone with contempt. It is used of the Assyrian king's words against the LORD (2 Kings 19:6, 22). Here the insult is in the people's acts of worship, set out in verse 28.

decisions.choice: acting faithlessly: breaking faith, betraying a trust
decisions.reason: The word is used for unfaithfulness toward God and what belongs to him (14:13; 15:8; 17:20; 18:24). The Hebrew doubles it, "acting faithlessly with faithlessness", for emphasis.

decisions.choice: in this also: points forward to what verse 28 describes
decisions.reason: The rebellion in the wilderness has been told; "this also" is the further sin committed in the land itself.

records.heading: Offerings on every high hill

records.source: וָאֲבִיאֵם֙ אֶל־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָשָׂ֨אתִי֙ אֶת־יָדִ֔י לָתֵ֥ת אוֹתָ֖הּ לָהֶ֑ם וַיִּרְאוּ֩ כָל־גִּבְעָ֨ה רָמָ֜ה וְכָל־עֵ֣ץ עָבֹ֗ת וַיִּזְבְּחוּ־שָׁ֤ם אֶת־זִבְחֵיהֶם֙ וַיִּתְּנוּ־שָׁם֙ כַּ֣עַס קָרְבָּנָ֔ם וַיָּשִׂ֣ימוּ שָׁ֗ם רֵ֚יחַ נִיח֣וֹחֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּסִּ֥יכוּ שָׁ֖ם אֶת־נִסְכֵּיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I brought them to the land that I lifted my hand to give it to them, and they saw every hill high and every tree leafy, and they sacrificed there their sacrifices, and they gave there [the] provocation of their offering, and they set there [the] aroma of their soothing, and they poured out there their drink offerings.
pieces: When I brought them into the land I had sworn to give them, wherever they saw a high hill or a leafy tree, they offered their sacrifices there. There they presented offerings that provoked {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, there they sent up their soothing aromas, and there they poured out their drink offerings.

L.28: When I had brought them into the land which I lifted {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to give them, and they saw every high hill and every leafy tree, and they offered their sacrifices there, and they presented there the provocation of their offering, and they set there their soothing aroma, and they poured out their drink offerings there.

R.28: I brought them into the land I had promised with an oath to give them. But whenever they saw a high hill or a tree with thick leaves, they offered their sacrifices there. They made offerings there that made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry. They burned sweet-smelling offerings there and poured out drink offerings.

decisions.choice: every high hill and every leafy tree: the places of the hill shrines
decisions.reason: Hilltops and green trees were the sites of Canaanite worship, which Israel was told to destroy (Deuteronomy 12:2) and then took up (1 Kings 14:23; Jeremiah 2:20). Ezekiel names them in 6:13 as places where the idols were given offerings.

decisions.choice: the provocation of their offering: offerings that provoked God to anger
decisions.reason: The word for provocation means vexation, what stirs someone to anger. The offerings were meant to please, but made to idols they provoked the LORD (8:17; Deuteronomy 32:16).

decisions.choice: soothing aroma: the smell of a sacrifice that pleases
decisions.reason: This is the language of the law for an offering God accepts (Genesis 8:21; Leviticus 1:9). Here it is offered to idols, as in 6:13 and 16:19. In verse 41 God will accept the people themselves "as a soothing aroma".

decisions.choice: offerings that provoked me
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the phrase means (m2); Literal keeps it as it is. The Hebrew's fourfold "there" is kept at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם מָ֣ה הַבָּמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֥ם הַבָּאִ֖ים שָׁ֑ם וַיִּקָּרֵ֤א שְׁמָהּ֙ בָּמָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And I said to them, What [is] the high place that you [are] going there? And was called its name Bamah to the day the this.
pieces: I asked them, "What is this high place you go to?" And it is still called Bamah to this day.

L.29: And I said to them, "What [is] the high place to which you go?" And its name is called Bamah to this day.

R.29: I asked them, "What is this hilltop shrine you keep going to?" People still call such a place a Bamah, a hilltop shrine, to this day.

decisions.choice: What is the high place you go to?: a mocking play on the word "bamah"
alternatives: a plain question about one particular shrine
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sounds out "what" (mah), "the high place" (habbamah) and "you go" (habba'im), as though the word bamah meant "go-what". The question scorns the shrines: what is this place that you keep going to? How the last sentence, that it is called Bamah to this day, fits the play is not certain; it may mean that the name itself still witnesses against them.

decisions.choice: Bamah: a local shrine, often on a height
decisions.reason: A bamah, usually translated "high place", was a local place of worship with an altar, often on a hill. Some were used for the LORD's worship before the temple was built (1 Kings 3:2-4); later kings tore them down as places of idolatry (2 Kings 23:8, 13).

decisions.choice: Bamah, kept as a name (L, B); a Bamah, a hilltop shrine (R)
decisions.reason: The sentence is about a name, so Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew word. Readable explains it in the text with the book's Readable word, "hilltop shrine", and makes plain that the name is used for all such places.

records.source: לָכֵ֞ן אֱמֹ֣ר׀אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הַבְּדֶ֥רֶךְ אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם אַתֶּ֣ם נִטְמְאִ֑ים וְאַחֲרֵ֥י שִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֖ם אַתֶּ֥ם זֹנִֽים׃
records.gloss: Therefore say to [the] house of Israel, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: In [the] way of your fathers [are] you defiling yourselves, and after their detestable things [are] you prostituting yourselves?
pieces: Therefore say to the house of Israel, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Will you make yourselves unclean as your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} did, and prostitute yourselves by running after their vile idols?

L.30: Therefore say to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Are you defiling yourselves in the way of your fathers, and prostituting yourselves after their detestable things?

R.30: So tell the people of Israel, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Will you make yourselves unclean, as your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} did? Will you be unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, like a woman with many lovers, and chase after their disgusting idols?

decisions.choice: prostituting yourselves: worshiping other gods, pictured as a wife's unfaithfulness
decisions.reason: The prophets speak of Israel's worship of other gods as a wife's prostitution (Hosea 4:12; Jeremiah 3:1). Ezekiel develops the picture at length in chapters 16 and 23; see the note at 16:1.

decisions.choice: the question is an accusation: you are doing just what your ancestors did
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "yes". The present generation, including the elders sitting before Ezekiel, has carried on the sins of the generations the chapter has listed.

decisions.choice: be unfaithful to me, like a woman with many lovers
decisions.reason: The verb follows the wording set for Ezekiel: "prostitute oneself" at Literal and Balanced, and "be unfaithful, like a woman with many lovers" at Readable, as in Jeremiah 3:1.

records.source: וּבִשְׂאֵ֣ת מַתְּנֹֽתֵיכֶ֡ם בְּֽהַעֲבִיר֩ בְּנֵיכֶ֨ם בָּאֵ֜שׁ אַתֶּם֩ נִטְמְאִ֤֨ים לְכָל־גִּלּֽוּלֵיכֶם֙ עַד־הַיּ֔וֹם וַאֲנִ֛י אִדָּרֵ֥שׁ לָכֶ֖ם בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל חַי־אָ֗נִי נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה אִם־אִדָּרֵ֖שׁ לָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And in the lifting up of your gifts, in making your sons pass through the fire, you [are] defiling yourselves to all your idols to this day; and I, shall I be inquired of by you, house of Israel? [As] I live, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, I will not be inquired of by you.
pieces: When you offer your gifts and make your {{gender:children|sons}} pass through the fire, you are making yourselves unclean with all your idols to this very day. House of Israel, should I then let you consult {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? As surely as I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, you will get no answer from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.31: And when you offer your gifts, when you make your {{gender:children|sons}} pass through the fire, you are defiling yourselves with all your filthy idols to this day. And am I to be inquired of by you, house of Israel? As I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, I will not be inquired of by you.

R.31: Even today you make yourselves unclean by offering gifts to all your idols and by burning your {{gender:children|sons}} as sacrifices. People of Israel, should I answer you when you come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? As surely as I live, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, I will not answer you.

decisions.choice: making children pass through the fire: child sacrifice
decisions.reason: The phrase is used for the sacrifice of children by fire to other gods (2 Kings 16:3; 21:6; 23:10; Jeremiah 32:35), which the law forbids (Leviticus 18:21; Deuteronomy 18:10). Jeremiah 7:31 says plainly that children were burned in the fire. The Hebrew says "sons"; the practice took daughters too (Jeremiah 7:31).

decisions.choice: the answer to verse 3
decisions.reason: The chapter returns to its start: the elders came to consult the LORD, and he will not be consulted by people who are still doing what their ancestors did.

decisions.choice: burning your children as sacrifices
alternatives: making your children pass through the fire
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the phrase means (m1). Every level has "children", with "sons" as the alternative.

records.source: וְהָֽעֹלָה֙ עַל־ר֣וּחֲכֶ֔ם הָי֖וֹ לֹ֣א תִֽהְיֶ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֗ים נִֽהְיֶ֤ה כַגּוֹיִם֙ כְּמִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת הָאֲרָצ֔וֹת לְשָׁרֵ֖ת עֵ֥ץ וָאָֽבֶן׃
records.gloss: And what comes up on your spirit, surely it will not be, [you] who say, We will be like the nations, like the clans of the lands, to serve wood and stone.
pieces: What you have in mind will never happen, when you say, "We will be like the nations, like the peoples of other lands, who worship wood and stone."

L.32: And what comes up into your mind will never come about, when you say, "We will be like the nations, like the clans of the lands, serving wood and stone."

R.32: You say, "We want to be like the nations and the peoples of other lands, who worship gods made of wood and stone." But what you are thinking will never happen.

decisions.choice: what comes up on your spirit: what you are thinking and planning
decisions.reason: The spirit here is the mind. 11:5 uses the same idiom: "I know what comes up in your spirit".

decisions.choice: serving wood and stone: worshiping idols, as the law warned exiles would
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 4:28 and 28:36, 64 warn that in exile Israel would serve gods of wood and stone. The exiles now propose to do it by choice: to stop being a people set apart and to live like everyone else.

decisions.choice: the saying first, then the answer
decisions.reason: Readable puts what the people say first, so the answer "it will never happen" comes after the thing it denies. It adds "gods made of" to say what serving wood and stone means.

records.source: חַי־אָ֕נִי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה אִם־לֹ֠א בְּיָ֨ד חֲזָקָ֜ה וּבִזְר֧וֹעַ נְטוּיָ֛ה וּבְחֵמָ֥ה שְׁפוּכָ֖ה אֶמְל֥וֹךְ עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: [As] I live, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, surely with a hand strong and with an arm outstretched and with wrath poured out I will be king over you.
pieces: As surely as I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and with wrath poured out, I will rule over you as king.

L.33: As I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, surely with a strong hand and with an arm stretched out and with wrath poured out I will be king over you.

R.33: As surely as I live, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, I will rule over you as your king. I will use all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power against you and pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on you.

decisions.choice: a strong hand and an outstretched arm: the words of the exodus, now with "wrath poured out"
decisions.reason: "A strong hand and an outstretched arm" describe God's power in bringing Israel out of Egypt (Deuteronomy 4:34; 5:15; 26:8). Adding "with wrath poured out" turns the words of rescue into words of judgment, as Jeremiah 21:5 does.

decisions.choice: I will be king over you: God will not let his people go their own way
decisions.reason: This answers verse 32. The exiles want to be like the nations; God insists on remaining their king, even if it means ruling them through judgment.

decisions.choice: I will use all my power against you and pour out my anger on you
alternatives: with a strong hand and an outstretched arm
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of hand and arm means, as Exodus 6:6 does at Readable.

records.source: וְהוֹצֵאתִ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ מִן־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים וְקִבַּצְתִּ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם מִן־הָ֣אֲרָצ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר נְפוֹצֹתֶ֖ם בָּ֑ם בְּיָ֤ד חֲזָקָה֙ וּבִזְר֣וֹעַ נְטוּיָ֔ה וּבְחֵמָ֖ה שְׁפוּכָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands where you were scattered among them, with a hand strong and with an arm outstretched and with wrath poured out.
pieces: I will bring you out from among the peoples and gather you out of the countries where you have been scattered, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and with wrath poured out.

L.34: And I will bring you out from among the peoples and gather you from the lands in which you have been scattered, with a strong hand and with an arm stretched out and with wrath poured out.

R.34: I will bring you out from the nations and gather you from the countries where you have been scattered. I will use all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power and pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger as I do it.

decisions.choice: I will bring you out and gather you: a new exodus
decisions.reason: The verb "bring out" is the verb of the exodus from Egypt (verses 6, 9, 10). Other prophets also speak of the return from exile as a second exodus (Isaiah 11:11-16; Jeremiah 23:7-8).

decisions.choice: with wrath poured out: the gathering leads to judgment
alternatives: wrath against the nations that held Israel
decisions.reason: The same words as verse 33 show that the new exodus is not only rescue. As verses 35-38 explain, God gathers his people in order to judge them and purge out the rebels.

records.source: וְהֵבֵאתִ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֶל־מִדְבַּ֖ר הָֽעַמִּ֑ים וְנִשְׁפַּטְתִּ֤י אִתְּכֶם֙ שָׁ֔ם פָּנִ֖ים אֶל־פָּנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And I will bring you into [the] wilderness of the peoples, and I will enter into judgment with you there face to face.
pieces: I will lead you into the wilderness of the peoples, and there I will judge you face to face.

L.35: And I will lead you into the wilderness of the peoples, and I will contend in judgment with you there face to face.

R.35: I will take you into a desert among the nations. There I will judge you face to face.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of the peoples: a new wilderness, like Sinai's, on the way out of exile
alternatives: the desert between Babylon and the land of Israel
decisions.reason: The phrase is found only here. As Israel once passed through the wilderness on the way from Egypt, so the exiles will pass through a wilderness among the nations on their way home, and there they will meet God in judgment. Whether a real desert is meant, such as the one between Babylon and Israel, or the picture is drawn wholly from the first exodus, the text does not say.

decisions.choice: face to face: as at Sinai, now in judgment
decisions.reason: At Sinai God spoke with Israel "face to face" (Deuteronomy 5:4). The meeting will be just as direct, but this time it is a trial.

decisions.choice: a desert among the nations
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture in plain words and does not decide where the desert is (m1).

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר נִשְׁפַּ֨טְתִּי֙ אֶת־אֲב֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם בְּמִדְבַּ֖ר אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם כֵּ֚ן אִשָּׁפֵ֣ט אִתְּכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: Just as I entered into judgment with your fathers in [the] wilderness of [the] land of Egypt, so I will enter into judgment with you, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: As I judged your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so I will judge you, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.36: As I contended with your fathers in judgment in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, in the same way I will contend in judgment with you, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.36: I judged your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} in the desert after they left Egypt. In the same way I will judge you, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: judgment in the wilderness: the generation that died before reaching the land
decisions.reason: The adults who left Egypt died in the wilderness and did not enter the land (Numbers 14:20-35; verse 15). The exiles will face the same sorting.

decisions.choice: in the desert after they left Egypt
alternatives: in the wilderness of the land of Egypt
decisions.reason: The wilderness meant is the one Israel crossed after leaving Egypt, so Readable says so.

records.source: וְהַעֲבַרְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑בֶט וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּמָסֹ֥רֶת הַבְּרִֽית׃
records.gloss: And I will make you pass under the rod and bring you into [the] bond of the covenant.
pieces: I will make you pass under the shepherd's rod and bring you into the bond of the covenant.

L.37: And I will make you pass under the rod and bring you into the bond of the covenant.

R.37: I will count you one by one, as a shepherd counts sheep that pass under his staff. I will bring you into the covenant and hold you to it.

decisions.choice: pass under the rod: as a shepherd counts and checks his sheep
decisions.reason: A shepherd counted his flock by making the sheep pass one by one under his staff (Leviticus 27:32; Jeremiah 33:13). God will examine each of his people in the same way, choosing some and setting others apart (verse 38).

decisions.choice: the bond of the covenant: the Hebrew text, taking a rare word as "bond", from the verb "to bind"
alternatives: "I will bring you in by number" (the Septuagint, which seems to read a similar Hebrew word and has nothing for "of the covenant")
decisions.reason: The word for "bond" is found only here. It is usually taken from the verb "to bind", like the bonds of a yoke. The Greek reads "by number", which would fit the counting of the sheep; the Hebrew makes good sense and is followed.

decisions.choice: the shepherd's rod
decisions.reason: Balanced names the shepherd so that the reader does not think of a rod for beating (m1). Readable makes the counting explicit and turns the "bond" into God holding the people to the covenant.

records.source: וּבָרוֹתִ֣י מִכֶּ֗ם הַמֹּרְדִ֤ים וְהַפּֽוֹשְׁעִים֙ בִּ֔י מֵאֶ֤רֶץ מְגֽוּרֵיהֶם֙ אוֹצִ֣יא אוֹתָ֔ם וְאֶל־אַדְמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֣א יָב֑וֹא וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will purge from you the rebels and the transgressors against me; from [the] land of their sojourning I will bring them out, but to [the] land of Israel he will not enter, and you will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: I will purge from among you those who revolt and rebel against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will bring them out of the country where they are living as foreigners, but not one of them will set foot in Israel's land. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.38: And I will purge from among you the rebels and those who transgress against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; out of the land where they live as foreigners I will bring them, but they will not enter the land of Israel; and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.38: I will remove from among you those who rebel and sin against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will bring them out of the countries where they are living as foreigners, but none of them will ever reach Israel's land. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: brought out, but not brought in: like the wilderness generation
decisions.reason: The rebels will leave the lands of exile like everyone else, but, like those who died in the wilderness (Numbers 14:29-30), they will not reach the land. The verb "enter" is singular: not one of them.

decisions.choice: the land of their sojourning: where they live as resident foreigners
decisions.reason: The word is used for the life of the patriarchs as foreigners in Canaan and Egypt (Genesis 17:8; 47:9). The exiles live in Babylon in the same way: as guests, not as citizens.

decisions.choice: you will know that I am the LORD: the refrain of the book
decisions.reason: The words, which Ezekiel uses over seventy times, say the purpose of God's acts of judgment and of rescue; see the note at 6:7.

decisions.choice: rebels and those who transgress (L); those who revolt and rebel (B); those who rebel and sin (R)
decisions.reason: The verb for transgressing follows the wording settled for the prophets: "transgress" (L), "rebel" (B), "sin" (R). Balanced uses "revolt" for the first word so that the two words stay distinct.

records.source: וְאַתֶּ֨ם בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה אִ֤ישׁ גִּלּוּלָיו֙ לְכ֣וּ עֲבֹ֔דוּ וְאַחַ֕ר אִם־אֵינְכֶ֖ם שֹׁמְעִ֣ים אֵלָ֑י וְאֶת־שֵׁ֤ם קָדְשִׁי֙ לֹ֣א תְחַלְּלוּ־ע֔וֹד בְּמַתְּנֽוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם וּבְגִלּוּלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you, house of Israel, thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Each [one] his idols go serve, and afterward, if you [are] not listening to me — but my holy name you will not profane any more with your gifts and with your idols.
pieces: As for you, house of Israel, the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Go, then, every one of you, and serve your idols, now and later, if you will not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. But you will no longer dishonor {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name with your gifts and your idols.

L.39: And as for you, house of Israel, thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Go, serve each [of you] his filthy idols, and afterward too, if you will not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name you will no longer profane with your gifts and with your filthy idols.

R.39: People of Israel, this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: If you will not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, then go ahead, all of you, and serve your idols, now and from now on. But you will not dishonor {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name any longer with your gifts and your idols.

decisions.choice: an ironic permission to serve idols, with a sentence that breaks off, and then a firm "no more"
alternatives: "Go, serve your idols; but afterward you will surely listen to me, and no longer profane my holy name" (taking the "if not" as an oath form meaning "surely")
"serve your idols, and afterward, since you do not listen to me, ..." with the threat left unsaid
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is hard. It begins with a bitter command, "Go, serve your idols", like Jeremiah 44:25 and Amos 4:4. The words "and afterward, if you are not listening to me" can be read as the second half of the irony ("go on doing it, if you will not listen"), or, since "if not" is a form used in oaths, as a promise that afterward they will listen. The last clause then says what must end: they will no longer profane God's name by mixing his worship with idols. The drafting follows the first reading; the promise of verses 40-44 is close to the second, and both end in a people who no longer profane the name.

decisions.choice: my holy name: God himself, as he is known
decisions.reason: To profane the name is to drag God's reputation down by worshiping him alongside idols (36:20-23; Leviticus 20:3).

decisions.choice: the condition first: "If you will not listen to me, then go ahead ..."
decisions.reason: Readable puts the condition before the command so that the irony is clear.

records.source: כִּ֣י בְהַר־קָדְשִׁ֞י בְּהַ֣ר׀מְר֣וֹם יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה שָׁ֣ם יַעַבְדֻ֜נִי כָּל־בֵּ֧ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל כֻּלֹּ֖ה בָּאָ֑רֶץ שָׁ֣ם אֶרְצֵ֔ם וְשָׁ֞ם אֶדְר֣וֹשׁ אֶת־תְּרוּמֹֽתֵיכֶ֗ם וְאֶת־רֵאשִׁ֛ית מַשְׂאוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם בְּכָל־קָדְשֵׁיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: For on my holy mountain, on [the] mountain [of the] height of Israel, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, there will serve me all [the] house of Israel, all of it, in the land; there I will accept them, and there I will require your contributions and the first of your gifts, with all your holy things.
pieces: For on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain, Israel's high mountain, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, there in the land the whole house of Israel, every one of them, will serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. There I will accept them, and there I will require your contributions and your choicest gifts, with all your holy offerings.

L.40: For on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain, on the mountain of the height of Israel, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, there in the land all the house of Israel, all of it, will serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; there I will accept them, and there I will seek your contributions and the first of your gifts, with all your holy things.

R.40: On {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain, the high mountain of Israel, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, all the people of Israel will worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in their land. There I will accept them. There I will ask for your offerings, your best gifts and all your holy gifts.

decisions.choice: my holy mountain, the high mountain of Israel: Zion, the temple mount
decisions.reason: Ezekiel calls the place of the future temple "a high and lofty mountain" (17:22-23) and sees the temple vision from "a very high mountain" (40:2). Isaiah 2:2 likewise pictures the LORD's mountain raised above the hills. In contrast to the many hill shrines of verse 28, there will be one place of worship.

decisions.choice: contributions and the first of your gifts: offerings set apart for God
decisions.reason: The first word is used for gifts lifted off and set aside for the sanctuary (Exodus 25:2; Numbers 18:8). "The first" can mean the first portion or the best; both show that God is given the best.

decisions.choice: all the house of Israel, all of it: the whole people, north and south together
decisions.reason: The emphasis looks ahead to 37:15-22, where Israel and Judah become one people again.

decisions.choice: the high mountain of Israel
alternatives: the mountain of the height of Israel
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the Hebrew phrase in ordinary English; Literal keeps its form. Readable uses "worship" for "serve", which here means serving God in worship.

records.source: בְּרֵ֣יחַ נִיחֹחַ֮ אֶרְצֶ֣ה אֶתְכֶם֒ בְּהוֹצִיאִ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ מִן־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים וְקִבַּצְתִּ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם מִן־הָ֣אֲרָצ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר נְפֹצֹתֶ֖ם בָּ֑ם וְנִקְדַּשְׁתִּ֥י בָכֶ֖ם לְעֵינֵ֥י הַגּוֹיִֽם׃
records.gloss: With an aroma soothing I will accept you, when I bring you out from among the peoples and gather you from the lands in which you were scattered among them; and I will be shown holy in you in [the] eyes of the nations.
pieces: I will accept you as a soothing aroma when I bring you out from among the peoples and gather you from the countries where you have been scattered, and through you I will show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} holy in the sight of the nations.

L.41: As a soothing aroma I will accept you, when I bring you out from among the peoples and gather you from the lands in which you have been scattered; and I will be shown holy in you in the eyes of the nations.

R.41: When I bring you out from the nations and gather you from the countries where you were scattered, I will accept you as gladly as a pleasing offering. I will use you to show the nations that I am holy.

decisions.choice: as a soothing aroma: God will accept the people themselves like a sacrifice that pleases him
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one used for sacrifices in verse 28 (Genesis 8:21; Leviticus 1:9). Then it described offerings to idols; now the restored people are themselves the offering God delights in.

decisions.choice: I will be shown holy in you: God's holiness made plain to the nations through what he does for Israel
decisions.reason: Israel's sin had profaned God's name among the nations (verses 9, 14, 22); its restoration will show them that he is holy. Ezekiel says this again in 28:25, 36:23 and 39:27.

decisions.choice: as gladly as a pleasing offering
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of the aroma means (m1).

records.source: וִֽידַעְתֶּם֙ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה בַּהֲבִיאִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֶל־אַדְמַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֶל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָשָׂ֨אתִי֙ אֶת־יָדִ֔י לָתֵ֥ת אוֹתָ֖הּ לַאֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will know that I [am] Yahweh, when I bring you to [the] land of Israel, to the land that I lifted my hand to give it to your fathers.
pieces: Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I have brought you to the land of Israel, the land I swore to give to your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}.

L.42: And you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I have brought you into the land of Israel, into the land that I lifted {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to give to your fathers.

R.42: Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I have brought you back into the land of Israel. It is the land I promised with an oath to give to your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}.

decisions.choice: the land sworn to the ancestors: the oath of verses 6 and 28 kept
decisions.reason: The oath that shut the rebels out (verses 15, 23) gives way to the oath first sworn to the ancestors (Exodus 6:8).

decisions.choice: bring you back
decisions.reason: The people addressed are exiles, so Readable says "back".

records.source: וּזְכַרְתֶּם־שָׁ֗ם אֶת־דַּרְכֵיכֶם֙ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־עֲלִיל֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִטְמֵאתֶ֖ם בָּ֑ם וּנְקֹֽטֹתֶם֙ בִּפְנֵיכֶ֔ם בְּכָל־רָעוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲשִׂיתֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will remember there your ways and all your deeds by which you defiled yourselves in them, and you will loathe yourselves in your faces for all your evils that you have done.
pieces: There you will remember your ways and all the deeds by which you made yourselves unclean, and you will loathe yourselves for all the evil you have done.

L.43: And there you will remember your ways and all your deeds by which you defiled yourselves, and you will loathe yourselves in your own sight for all the evil things that you have done.

R.43: There you will remember how you lived and all the things you did that made you unclean. You will hate yourselves for all the evil things you have done.

decisions.choice: loathe yourselves in your own sight: be disgusted with yourselves
decisions.reason: The same words are used in 6:9 and 36:31. Seeing themselves as they really were, the people will be ashamed of what they did.

decisions.choice: remorse after restoration
alternatives: remorse as a condition of restoration
decisions.reason: The people remember and loathe themselves after God has brought them home, not before. The order is the same in 16:61-63 and 36:31-32: God's undeserved kindness leads them to shame for their past.

records.source: וִֽידַעְתֶּם֙ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה בַּעֲשׂוֹתִ֥י אִתְּכֶ֖ם לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמִ֑י לֹא֩ כְדַרְכֵיכֶ֨ם הָרָעִ֜ים וְכַעֲלִילֽוֹתֵיכֶ֤ם הַנִּשְׁחָתוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And you will know that I [am] Yahweh, when I deal with you for the sake of my name, not according to your ways evil and according to your deeds corrupt, house of Israel, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, house of Israel, when I deal with you for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name and not as your evil ways and your corrupt deeds deserve, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.44: And you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I deal with you for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, not according to your evil ways nor according to your corrupt deeds, house of Israel, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.44: Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, people of Israel, when I deal with you to honor {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. I will not treat you as your evil ways and wicked deeds deserve, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: for the sake of my name: the refrain of verses 9, 14 and 22 now becomes the ground of mercy
decisions.reason: In the wilderness God held back judgment for his name's sake; at the end of the chapter he acts for his name's sake in a way their deeds never deserved. The chapter's last word is grace, not merit.

decisions.choice: chapter 20 ends here in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text this verse closes chapter 20, and chapter 21 begins with "The word of the LORD came to me" (Hebrew 21:1). Many Bibles number the next five verses 20:45-49; see the note at 21:1.

decisions.choice: house of Israel, placed after the refrain
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable move the address to the start so that the long sentence ends with what God will not do and with the closing formula.
